help.title: Hamstrung
help.help: Hamstring has crippled the target’s stride: movement is reduced, but its attack cadence is unchanged. It can still attack and cast; this is soft control, not a root or stun.

help.title: Bound
help.help: Binding Strike has pinned the target in place. It can still attack anything already in reach, but cannot reposition until the bind ends.

help.title: Stunned
help.help: The target cannot move or act until this hard-control window ends. This is the control applied by Stunning Strike or a frost shatter; slow resistance does not help.

help.title: Vulnerable
help.help: The target takes amplified damage from every source while this holds.

help.title: Shred
help.help: Plating stripped from the target. Every hit landed on it — yours and your party’s — has that much less flat damage removed.

target.source: the Poison Dagger's own poison reservoir (weaponDot, 50% of the hit over 4.5 s) — not a card, but on the same target
target.label: Poison

help.title: Poison
help.help: A weapon reservoir: a pool of poison damage stored on the target that drains into it over time. The badge counts damage still owed, not stacks.

target.source: the Striker's class bleed — an affliction the Affliction moment also finds
target.label: Bleed

help.title: Bleed
help.help: The target is bleeding: damage over time applied by your rhythm, past its plating.

target.source: the Apprentice's class DoT — an affliction the Affliction moment also finds
target.label: DoT

help.title: Damage over time
help.help: Your damage-over-time is working on this target. It bypasses plating entirely and only half the target’s damage reduction applies, so it is your answer to heavily armoured enemies.

help.title: Surge
help.help: A lineage card opened a damage window. Your hits land harder until it closes — the same one-multiplier-per-hit slot an empowered attack uses, so it does not stack a second multiplier on top.

help.title: Wake
help.help: A lineage card opened an attack-speed window. It adds to Frenzy and any stance window rather than replacing them.

help.title: Mend
help.help: A lineage card switched on a share of your Recovery rate for a window. What that converts to in HP depends on your Recovery stat.

help.title: Brace
help.help: A lineage card opened a damage-reduction window — opening protection, earned by how the card fires rather than by gear.

help.title: Shell
help.help: A lineage card granted a temporary absorb pool, spent before your barrier and your health.

help.title: Plate
help.help: A lineage card is adding plating to each reactive-plating stack you are holding. The stacks themselves still build from hits taken and fade one at a time.

help.title: Form
help.help: A Technique lineage card opened a window: the next Technique that lands does so empowered, and the window closes when it spends. It uses the same one-multiplier-per-hit slot an empowered attack does, so a Technique rider adds to it rather than multiplying with it.

help.title: Slip
help.help: A lineage card opened an evasion window: for its duration, a chance to graze a hit (take half of it) on top of whatever your gear already gives you. A graze still lets the monster's ailments through.

help.title: Frame window
help.help: Your frame’s mechanic just fired and opened its window. It is deliberately shorter than one full cycle, so the faster you attack the more of each cycle you spend inside it — your frame tile says what the window is doing while it counts down.

help.title: Frame charge
help.help: Your frame is banking charge, one per regular hit, up to the cap shown. Your mechanic spends the whole bank when it fires and makes that one hit bigger — it is not a second multiplier stacked on top, it is the same multiplier grown.

rhythm.note: rhythmReadoutModel.ts: one ring per active triggered card (at most three, with the frame ring). Shapes: count = k/n toward hit-nth; cap = a clock after firing, ✦ when ready; latch-body = ✦ ready on this target, — spent; carry = ✦ armed by a kill, — waiting; pulse = • resting.
